slots.brief: Calorimetry with phase change: ice at 0°C added to warm water; find final temperature or mass of ice melted using latent heat and specific heat, comparing the heat lost and gained.
Massive rope (or Atwood variant) over a frictionless pulley in the diagram; write equations for both bodies and solve for acceleration or tension symbolically, with a light connecting segment.

slots.subtopic: First law; path independence of internal energy
slots.brief: First law; path independence of internal energy: state which quantities (ΔU, Q, W) depend only on initial/final states across two different paths between the same states.
Magnetic flux through a stationary loop changes linearly with time (uniform field growing/shrinking); compute average induced emf and current through a resistance over a time interval.
A man walks on the rim of a freely spinning stationary platform (disc); use conservation of angular momentum to find final angular velocity ratio from moments of inertia.

slots.subtopic: Interference – mirror images as coherent sources
slots.brief: Mirror images as coherent sources: point source near a mirror acting as a double-slit geometry; find fringe width or phase difference at a point using path-difference geometry.

Hard conceptual MCQ on elastic behaviour: compare stress-strain curves / breaking stress vs elastic limit of two wires of different lengths and cross-sections, identifying which statements about Young's modulus, elongation and breaking load hold true.
Radioactive decay: given fraction of a sample remaining after a given time, determine the half-life; or given half-life determine number of half-lives in a stated activity-drop period.
Charge sharing: two capacitors at different voltages connected in parallel; compute common voltage and energy lost as heat, comparing initial and final stored energies.
Forward-biased diode in a DC circuit: silicon diode in series/parallel with resistors (circuit diagram given); use the 0.7 V drop to find branch currents and voltage across a resistor.
Excess pressure in soap bubbles: two soap bubbles of different radii in contact or compared; use 4T/r (or 2T/r distinction between a bubble and a drop) to find a ratio of excess pressures.

Binary/circular orbit: a satellite or two-body system in circular orbit; use energy conservation to relate total energy, kinetic energy and potential energy of an orbiting mass, or compute escape-speed change from a stated orbit radius.

Energy in SHM: a horizontal or vertical spring–mass oscillator; find displacement from the mean where kinetic energy equals potential energy, or compute amplitude from a given speed at a given displacement.
Helical motion: a charged particle enters at an angle to a uniform magnetic field; compute radius of the helix and time period of revolution, and compare with the perpendicular-entry case.

Dimensional analysis: given a physics equation involving a new/defined quantity (e.g. coefficient of viscosity, Planck-like constant), find the dimensional formula of the unknown constant by dimensional homogeneity of all terms.

slots.subtopic: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves
slots.brief: Radiation pressure / momentum of EM waves: conceptual MCQ on how radiation pressure and momentum density change when a wave is fully absorbed vs fully reflected by a surface.

Cell combinations (circuit diagram): cells with emf and internal resistance connected in series/parallel across an external load; find current and terminal voltage, comparing with the equivalent-cell approach.
Field from potential: a given potential function V(x,y) or potential along a line; differentiate to get the field and evaluate the vector direction at a specified point.

Hard logic-gate circuit: a multi-gate combination (e.g. NANDs feeding an output gate) described or as a Boolean expression; reduce to identify the equivalent single gate and evaluate output for a truth-table row, with a diagram of gates.
Area under v-t graph: a piecewise-linear or triangular v–t curve described numerically; read off acceleration from slope and displacement from area, including a retarding segment.

slots.subtopic: Work done by friction on incline
slots.brief: Work-energy theorem with a diagram: block sliding down a rough incline or released from a height with friction; use energy conservation between initial and final heights to find speed at the bottom or work done against friction.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.subtopic: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges
slots.brief: de Broglie wavelength of accelerated charges: an electron and a proton (or same particle through two different potentials); compare de Broglie wavelengths using the ratio for equal KE vs equal momentum.
Series LCR at resonance (circuit given): state resonance condition and compute rms current, or identify power factor and phase relation between V and I at resonance.

Angular momentum of a particle about a point: given position and velocity (or momentum) vectors, compute L = r × p magnitude and direction using the cross product; keep it distinct from the other rotational slot (conservation question).

slots.subtopic: Mean free path / mean free time
slots.brief: Hard statement-evaluation MCQ mixing gas laws and kinetic theory: assess which statements about rms speed, mean free path, degrees of freedom and pressure of an ideal gas are true, including a non-obvious one (e.g. mean free path independent of temperature at constant pressure).
Energy level transitions in hydrogen-like atom: find the wavelength or energy ratio of photons emitted in a stated transition series, or compute the shortest wavelength of a spectral series.
Doppler effect: a source and observer moving relative to each other (both approach, or one recedes); compute the apparent frequency heard, or ratio of approach to recede frequencies.
Prism / mirror combination: two thin prisms in contact giving deviation without dispersion; use ω and net deviation conditions, or solve two equations in two unknowns for the prism angles.

Projectile motion: ball thrown at an angle or dropped from a moving platform; combine the two perpendicular kinematic equations to find time of flight and range (or landing position), with simple given numbers.

Circular motion with friction: a car on a level or banked curve (diagram shows forces); resolve forces along radial and vertical directions to find maximum speed without slipping, or minimum coefficient of friction.
Give three statements comparing d^4/d^6 octahedral complexes in weak vs strong field (spin state, unpaired electrons, spin-only moment) and ask which combination is correct.
Gaseous AB-type dissociation set up as an ICE table; from total equilibrium pressure find degree of dissociation and then Kp.
Given standard potentials of two couples involving a common metal, compute E° of the cell formed by combining them.
Rank four alkyl halides (including allylic and aryl halides) in order of their rate of solvolysis via SN1.
Match water-soluble and fat-soluble vitamins with their deficiency diseases or sources.
From a list of aqueous ions (including d^0 and d^10 cases), pick which are colourless, coded as 1/2/3/4 combinations.
Arrange four species (with varying lone pairs and multiple bonds, e.g. water, ammonia, carbonyl-type, amide-type) in order of decreasing bond angle with justification from VSEPR.
Combustion of an organic compound containing C, H and O: from masses of CO2 and H2O collected, deduce percentage of oxygen and then the molecular formula using an independent molar-mass clue.
Evaluate statements on gold number, protective action of lyophilic sols, and Hardy–Schulze rule for coagulation; pick the incorrect one.
For a given 3d-series ion, write the d-electron configuration, count unpaired electrons and compute the spin-only magnetic moment.
Identify the carbonyl fragments obtained on reductive ozonolysis of a substituted alkene.
Match common artificial sweeteners (e.g. aspartame, sucralose, alitame, saccharin) with their structural features or use-limits.
From a set of primary, secondary and tertiary amines, identify which respond to the carbylamine test and which do not.
Compare rates or effusion times of two gases of known molar masses diffusing through the same pinhole.
Four orders of electron gain enthalpy (including Cl vs F and S vs O anomalies) are given; pick the incorrect one.
Statements comparing classical (reducing) smog and photochemical (oxidising) smog – constituents, time of formation, health effects; choose the correct set.
Predict the products when an unsymmetrical ether reacts with excess HI, highlighting the SN1 vs SN2 pathway depending on the alkyl groups.
Select the correct IUPAC name of a branched haloalkene with correct numbering and substituent order.
Compare radius or energy of the nth orbit of a hydrogen-like ion with that of hydrogen in the corresponding orbit, scaling with Z.
Give hydrolysis products of covalent halides such as NCl3 and PCl3/PCl5 and ask why they differ; combine the correct product sets and reasoning in one option set.
Figure shows an alcohol and a target ether; choose the best halide–alkoxide combination and conditions for a high-yield Williamson synthesis.
For a first-order reaction, find the time for a stated fraction of reactant to decompose, or the fraction left after a given number of half-lives.
From boiling-point elevation or freezing-point depression of a weak electrolyte solution with known molality, compute the van 't Hoff factor and then the degree of dissociation.
A complex with two different ligands and counter-ions is described; pick its fully correct IUPAC name with ligands in alphabetical order.
Figure displays four carbonyl structures (aldehyde, ketone, alpha-hydroxy ketone, carboxylic acid); identify which give a positive Tollens' or Fehling's test.
For a xenon fluoride (e.g. XeF4), determine the number of lone pairs on xenon, its hybridisation and the shape of the molecule.
Given limiting molar conductivities of a strong electrolyte pair, assemble the limiting molar conductivity of a weak acid (or base) by addition and subtraction of the values.
Figure shows a disubstituted benzene with one activating and one deactivating group; predict the major mononitration product considering the stronger director.
Figure shows Fischer projections of similar molecules; assign R/S at each stereocentre and classify pairs as identical, enantiomers or diastereomers.
Write the balanced combustion equation of a gaseous fuel, count Δng, and convert the given ΔH to ΔU (or vice versa) using ΔngRT.
Sentence split into parts (a/b/c/d) with a subject-verb agreement error (collective noun / distance-expression treated as singular); one option 'No error'.

slots.archetype: para jumble (5 sentences, find the first sentence)
slots.brief: Four sentence options given for the opening of a short paragraph on a general topic; pick the most coherent opener.
Single blank in a simple sentence; choose the word that fits context, options being near-synonyms of everyday level.
Pick the nearest meaning of a common NCERT-level word like 'obsolete' or 'candid' from four options.
Give the meaning of an idiom like 'to let the cat out of the bag' used in a short sentence.
Choose the opposite of a moderately common word such as 'abundant' or 'transparent'.
Underlined phrase with a tense inconsistency in a time-clause sentence (e.g., 'after he will finish'); pick the grammatically correct improvement.
Complete an analogy pair like 'Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?' with four options at a moderate difficulty level.
Give five similar-looking words and ask which one comes third when arranged as in a dictionary; brief the author to include words sharing first two letters so third-letter comparison matters.
A word is coded by shifting each letter a fixed number of positions forward; provide the coded form of one word and ask for the code of a second word at moderate difficulty.
Simple increasing series with a single constant pattern (e.g. add fixed number or alternate small steps); ask for the next term at the easiest level.
Pair of numbers related by a simple operation (e.g. square/cube, digit sum, or multiply-and-add constant); give one pair and a single number, ask for the analogous partner.

First pair maps a word/letter set to a numeric code using letter positional values combined with rearrangement of letters; candidate must decode the hidden two-step rule and apply it to a new word at highest difficulty.

Two straightforward universal/affirmative statements (All A are B, All B are C) with two conclusions; ask which conclusions definitely follow, keeping it at beginner level with no negatives or possibilities.
Series of letter groups where each term shifts forward by a fixed/increasing number of positions; ask for the next term, difficulty 2 with a mildly varying shift.
Statements with one negative or particular statement (Some A are not B type); conclusions include one definite deduction and one 'possibility' conclusion; ask which conclusions follow.
Give a medium-length word and four options; ask which option word can be formed using only the letters of the given word, each letter used at most as many times as it appears.

Four letter/number pairs where three share the same internal relation (e.g. same difference or product between pair members); pick the pair that does not follow, at moderate difficulty with a non-obvious common rule.
Simple direct letter coding: show a word written as a group of number codes and ask for the code of another word using the same letter-number mapping, kept easy with a short word.

Pointing-type question: a person says 'he is the son of my grandfather's only son/daughter' style single-step chain; ask how the pointed person is related to the speaker, using a short two-link chain.

Total number of students in a row and a student's position from one end is given; ask their position from the other end or how many are between two given ranks — keep it a one- or two-clause easy question.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image of a point in a given line and construct the equation of the line joining the point to its image.
Count arrangements of words where certain letters are never adjacent (complementary counting).
Find the condition on the radius/centre so that a circle is tangent to both coordinate axes or a given line.

slots.subtopic: Cross product and angle between vectors
slots.brief: Use the cross product of two vectors to find the sine of the angle between them, given their dot product.
Find the equation of a line through the intersection of two given lines and passing through another point (family of lines).
Evaluate a limit of the form (1 + kx)^(a/x) or (f(x))^g(x) reducing to e.
Find the domain of a function involving a square root of a quadratic expression using sign analysis.
Given a small frequency/univariate table, compute the mean deviation about the median.
Given a determinant with entries involving x, factorise it into linear factors using row/column operations.
Find the combined standard deviation of two groups given their sizes, means, and standard deviations.
Use differentials to estimate the approximate value of a root of a number or a function at a nearby point.
Sum an arithmetico-geometric series to n terms by multiplying by the common ratio and subtracting.
Use inclusion–exclusion to count the number of onto/surjective functions from one finite set to another.
Use z·z̄ = |z|² to simplify an expression involving conjugates and quotients into a real or simple form.
Solve a first-order linear ODE with a non-standard coefficient of dy/dx using the integrating factor method.
Determine k so that a piecewise function is continuous, then check differentiability at the joining point.
Given |f(x)| and g(x) counts for two sets, find the cardinality of the union or of a difference using Venn-style reasoning with three sets.
Solve a trigonometric equation of the form a cos x + b sin x = c or a sum-to-product type and write the general solution.
Use symmetry about the axis and the property ∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx with f(a−x) to evaluate a nontrivial definite integral without full antiderivatives.
Set up and compute the area bounded by a parabola/line pair or two curves with a simple intersection.
Find the work done / projection of one vector on another using dot product with given magnitudes and angle.
Bayes' theorem word problem: given prior probabilities and conditional probabilities, find the posterior probability of a cause.
Integrate a product (e.g., log or inverse trig function times polynomial/power) using integration by parts, possibly applied twice.
Solve a trigonometric equation involving multiple angles (e.g., tan 2x = cot 3x) and select the number of solutions in an interval or list the general solution.
Form 4-digit numbers from given digits satisfying a divisibility or repetition restriction, counting case by case.
For a matrix A satisfying a given quadratic matrix equation, express Aⁿ as a linear combination of A and I using repeated bookkeeping.
Use the scalar triple product/determinant condition to test whether three points or two lines and a point are coplanar, or find the shortest distance between skew lines.
Find the equation of a parabola (or its focus/directrix/latus rectum) from given vertex and axis information.
Solve a homogeneous differential equation dy/dx = f(y/x) using the substitution y = vx.
Convert a composite like sin⁻¹(x) expressed via tan⁻¹ into a single inverse trig value using the triangle method.
Find the direction cosines of a line joining two points, then the angle it makes with an axis, or the distance of a point from an axis.
Related rates: rate of change of volume/area given the rate of change of a length (sphere/cone/cube scenario).
Binomial distribution: find the probability of exactly/at least r successes, or recover the parameters given two probabilities.
Use the general term of (a + bx)ⁿ to find the coefficient of a specific power of x, or the term independent of x.
Identify the centre and radius of a circle by completing the square in its general equation.
Determine intervals where a polynomial/rational function is increasing or decreasing by sign analysis of f′(x).
Definite integral of a rational/trigonometric function where a substitution (t = tan x or x → 1/x) or symmetry simplifies it dramatically.
Classify a given relation (reflexive/symmetric/transitive/equivalence) on a small set and, if it is an equivalence, count equivalence classes.
Given a 3×3 matrix relationship between A, adj A and |A|, recover the missing determinant value, possibly with a diagonal or simple structured matrix.
Use Vieta's relations (sum/product of roots) of one quadratic to construct another quadratic whose roots are transformed (e.g., reciprocal or doubled roots).
